To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the momentum distributions of the valence quarks in the nucleon are peaked at large values of momentum and are not very sensitive to the specific form of the interquarks interaction, while the momentum distributions of valence quarks inside the prominent electro-produced nucleon resonances show a strong sensitivity to the interquarks potential; both the elastic and transition electromagnetic nucleon form factors are affected by the short-range part (i.e. the high-momentum components) of the interquarsk potential

the nucleon and nucleon resonance momentum distributions are characterized by a large content of high-momenta components, which are responsible for the large values of the electromagnetic form factors at high momentum transfers.

the momentum distributions of the quarks in the nucleon and its excited states, and the electromagnetic form factors of the nucleon and of the prominent nucleon resonances, are affected by the short-range part and the high-momentum components of the quark-antiquark interaction, which are responsible for the non-perturbativity of the strong interaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the investigation of the light-baryon spectroscopy and of the electromagnetic form factors in the quark model, with the main goal of providing a unified description of the low-energy hadronic processes, in particular of the nucleon-nucleon and of the pion-nucleon interaction, and of the nucleon structure.

the following topics: - the study of light-baryon spectra and electromagnetic form factors within the framework of the constituent quark models, with special attention to their high-momentum components. - the study of the light-baryon spectrum and electromagnetic form factors with the help of the light-front approach.
the study of the nucleon and of its prominent resonances within the framework of the quark potential model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both the valence + sea dominance and chiral symmetry breaking are important for the description of the nucleon and nucleon resonances in the quark model.

the quark model, with the above assumptions and approximations, is a useful tool in the analysis of light baryon spectroscopy, but it cannot be considered as a reliable, quantitative theory of the electromagnetic properties of the baryons.
the quark model provides a reasonable framework for describing both the nucleon and nucleon-resonance spectroscopy and for understanding the behaviour of the electromagnetic form factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the framework of the constituent quark picture, the observed nucleon resonances can be interpreted as quark-gluon excitations, but the nucleon structure is not a mere collection of free constituent quarks.

the quark model provides an adequate framework for understanding the structure and the spectroscopy of the light-baryon resonances, but the description of their properties, such as electromagnetic form factors, is still affected by a large uncertainty, due to the lack of an unambiguous prescription for the quark-gluon interaction and for the electromagnetic current.

the quark models, when properly applied, are able to provide a consistent description of both the nucleon and resonance spectra and of the corresponding electromagnetic form factors, at least up to Q 2 values of the order of 10 ÷20 (GeV/c)-2.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, at least for the electromagnetic form factors of the nucleon and its first resonances, it is possible to achieve a satisfactory description by using only the information provided by the quark wave functions, which can be calculated in a model-independent way from the quark potential models.

the quark model, in spite of its simplicity, can be used as a reliable tool for describing a large number of features of the light baryon spectroscopy, and can provide a useful guidance in the analysis of the experimental data on the electromagnetic form factors of the nucleon and its resonances.
the momentum distributions of the quarks in the nucleon and in the resonances can be reliably calculated within a quark potential model.
